indicators.note: the run of words encounter's eternal holds the letters within it

explanation.walkthrough: The quoted film title tempts as one unit, but 'Brief' is the definition and the letters run across encounTER'S Eternal.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is short and clipped, a synonym of brief.

indicators.note: turning the letters about stupidly means rattle on is rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A liberal outlook is a broad-minded, accepting one.

port is the nautical word for the left side of a ship

explanation.walkthrough: The 'special relationship' is the phrase for UK-US ties; here it is simply a definition of a close bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious understanding between people, which is any special relationship.

clue.text: Release when prison sentence is up

parts.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A prisoner is released when their sentence has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' sounds like the sentence ending, but in this down clue it turns TIME upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, so to release.

explanation.walkthrough: Black Sabbath was a famous heavy metal band, but here the words split into B and S, which go round RACKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackets are shelf supports fixed to a wall, holding things up.

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation sits inside the word for revival

parts.note: a cut is a stroke in cricket

clue.text: Former wife has enough following case

ample means plenty or enough

explanation.surface: An ex-wife has had enough of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a lawsuit; it means an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is an instance, a typical specimen.

clue.text: Girl when turning up in tabloid?

indicators.note: in means the reversed short word is placed inside the newspaper

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word from the bottom

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: A girl appearing in a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses the short word for when, as this is a down clue. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.

indicators.note: resolved, as in broken up and reformed, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective cries that an airtight case has been solved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes her detective novels, where cases are resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: The author is the famous writer of detective novels, the 'she' in question.

clue.text: Drink endless plonk with grand bird

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

parts.note: plonk is cheap wine
G is short for a grand, a thousand

explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing is a crested plover, a wading bird.

clue.text: "Blade" — a cult flick with heartless snipes?

explanation.walkthrough: 'flick' looks like a film, but it shuffles A CULT into CUTLA; 'heartless' keeps the first and last letters of snipes, SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short, curved sword, a type of blade.

clue.text: Queen and king circling round, round another piece

indicators.note: circling means the two royal letters go around the rest

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

a second O for the second round

explanation.surface: In chess, queen and king move around another piece on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'Queen' and 'king' look like pieces; R (Regina) and K surround two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is a chess piece, as are queen and king, hence another.

parts.note: a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Choosing a shade of cosmetic make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make up' reads as cosmetics but means make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, to make up for a wrong.

clue.text: Drew out the joke after getting point

indicators.note: after means the joke comes behind the point

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: Someone spun out a joke long after it had made its point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like the punchline, but it is a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out a story is to prolong or draw it out.

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for north sits inside the wave

parts.note: a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: Something swept northwards by a tidal surge.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore, such as the Severn Bore, is a wave travelling up an estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Borne is the past participle of bear, meaning carried.

clue.text: Sailor returning with a world plan

indicators.note: returning means the word for sailor is read backwards

parts.note: a salt, or old salt, is a seasoned sailor

explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the old salt backwards; 'world plan' is a whimsical definition of a book of maps.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, a plan of the world.

parts.note: a song played to make the whole people rise to their feet, read as if it sparked a revolt

explanation.surface: A rousing anthem meant to stir a revolution.

explanation.definitionFit: A country's official patriotic song, for which audiences rise.

definitions.meaning: to scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately
coal ... are metal buckets holding coal by the fire

explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately holing ships sinks them, and a coal bucket shares the same name.

indicators.note: flipping, read as turning over, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An indifferent person snaps at a pest to shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apathetic means lacking any interest or eagerness.

definitions.meaning: to have spotted is to have seen

explanation.definitionFit: Seen equals spotted, and split into two words it describes a plain cake lacking icing.

clue.text: Part of the massage after time working hard

indicators.note: after means the massage part is placed behind the time letter

parts.note: oiling the skin is part of a massage

explanation.surface: Rubbing oils during a massage takes some time and effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' suggests a hidden word, but it is just oiling as a step in a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiling means labouring hard.

indicators.note: before means the word for thrash comes ahead of the letter for hard

parts.note: to bat is to hit or strike
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A vigorous beating before going into the sauna, as in Finnish custom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Finnish sauna is followed by switching with birch twigs; here 'sauna, possibly' marks one kind of bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a type of steam bath, so an example.

indicators.note: in means the letter for good sits inside the word for nude

parts.note: bare means naked or nude

explanation.walkthrough: 'muscle' looks like a noun for physique, but it is the verb, to force your way in.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in or muscle in is to push your way in forcefully.

clue.text: Initially very important to all life

definitions.text: Initially very important to all life

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each following word

explanation.walkthrough: The bridge picture misleads: 'hand' is a clenched one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fist is a hand closed tight.

clue.text: Plant found by marsh around river

indicators.note: around means the marsh word is put round the letter for river

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land

explanation.surface: A plant growing beside a marsh near a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a leafy, flowerless plant.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a verb, stays; it is the noun, cremated ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels for holding the ashes of the cremated dead.

clue.text: Most substantial bosom on Rita's top half!

indicators.note: follows means the face comes after the shortened heart
mostly means the last letter of the word for heart is dropped

dial is slang for a person's face, and a clock face

explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and affable, a synonym of friendly.

indicators.note: rough, as in roughed up, signals that green and is rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to put it at risk, imperil it.

parts.note: ages are long times or eras

explanation.surface: Experts writing for the Sunday Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sunday Times is a British newspaper, but here the title splits into S and AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sages are wise people, experts whose opinions are sought.
